QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_49

question.text: Per Ch 4.3.1, the 'learning loop' in the Logic Model enables:

answer.text: Static, one-way execution with no feedback
Feedback and lessons from achieved or unachieved outputs and outcomes flowing back into activities, with periodic revision of assumptions and risks to refine project design over time
Exit of all stakeholders after year 1

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 95's learning-loop diagram shows that feedback and lessons from achieved or unachieved outputs and outcomes are incorporated back into activities. Page 96 reinforces this by discussing KPI information feeding periodic revision of assumptions and risks. Together they describe an iterative refinement of activities and project design, not a one-shot execution. The Trap: A denies the feedback mechanism altogether. C and D are unrelated to the workbook's learning-loop concept and introduce ideas (stakeholder exit, tax status) that are not part of the Logic Model. Note: The workbook describes the feedback flow as running from outputs and outcomes back into activities and as driving periodic refinement; it does not extend the loop all the way back to inputs, so that wording has been removed from the keyed answer.
